basis: Cerebellar degeneration and developmental impairment define disease; abnormal eye movements reflect neurologic dysfunction without intrinsic ocular damage.
Defining features are excessive hair growth, skeletal dysplasia and intellectual disability; no evidence for an endocrine disorder.
Myogenic weakness and congenital joint contractures define disease; normal nerve conduction and absent central involvement argue against a separate neurologic axis.
Dysmyelination establishes neurologic disease; defining jaundice suggests hepatic involvement, but its mechanism is unspecified in this sparse record.
Congenital abnormality of aortic arch position; associated compression or other malformations are not established as common intrinsic organ damage.
Disseminated melanoma, conventionally of cutaneous origin; origin is unspecified here. Meningeal disease is a subtype, so neurologic involvement is not generalized.
Congenital abdominal wall defect with exposed, herniated bowel defines disease; gastrointestinal morphology abnormalities occur in 30-79%.
Inherited apolipoprotein deficiency disrupts lipid metabolism; coronary atherosclerosis is a separately diagnosed consequence, and corneal arcus need not impair vision.
Endocrine-associated exophthalmic ophthalmoplegia represents immune-mediated orbital disease; thyroid gland dysfunction is not established by this ocular concept.
Inherited paroxysmal movement disorder; dystonia and associated swallowing or speech symptoms reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Hereditary prion-mediated neurodegeneration; infectious axis follows the transmissible prion disease classification. Abdominal symptoms do not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Neoplastic or non-neoplastic polyp arising in the stomach.
Developmental impairment and skeletal overgrowth abnormalities characterize syndrome; cataract reported in 1/1 supports ocular involvement, with limited frequency certainty.
Defined as nonsyndromic intellectual disability; singleton myopia and dental findings do not securely establish common intrinsic damage beyond the nervous system.
Substance-use disorder; no specific organ injury is part of this concept.
Malignant neoplasm of the urethra, included in the urinary axis; no common additional organ occupation is specified.
Benign neoplasm arising from the colon wall.
Trypanosoma infection umbrella; cardiac, gastrointestinal and neurologic damage differ across Chagas and African forms and are not common across the group.
Skeletal dysostosis, hearing loss and cleft palate define syndrome; ocular dysfunction occurs in 30-99%. Choanal atresia (30-79%) and nail defects (80-99%) omitted at cap.
Congenital lymphatic vascular malformation; hydrops and edema reflect drainage failure. Pleural and pericardial effusion frequencies and lasting organ damage are unspecified.
Hereditary skeletal muscle disease umbrella; dementia, ophthalmoplegia and respiratory muscle involvement vary by subtype. An immune mechanism is not implied.
Pontocerebellar malformation causes severe neurologic impairment; optic atrophy affects 4/8 patients. Dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction rather than intrinsic gut damage.
Immunodeficiency and congenital cardiomyopathy define the spectrum; hypoplastic spleen in 3/4 reported cases supports haematologic involvement. Evidence comes from two families.
Radial and ear defects define syndrome; cardiac defects 80-99%, renal defects 30-79%. Orofacial clefts and cognitive impairment (30-79%) omitted at cap.
Cardiomelic syndrome denotes congenital heart and limb malformations; the sparse record provides no support for additional organ involvement.
